title: My, your, this, that: possessives and demonstratives
summary: Mi, tu, su, nuestro… and este, ese, aquel: the little words before a noun.
focus: Possessive adjectives; de for possession; demonstratives este/ese/aquel
content:
## Possessive adjectives

| owner | singular noun | plural noun |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **mi** | **mis** |
| tú | **tu** | **tus** |
| él / ella / usted | **su** | **sus** |
| nosotros/as | **nuestro / nuestra** | **nuestros / nuestras** |
| vosotros/as | **vuestro / vuestra** | **vuestros / vuestras** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **su** | **sus** |

They agree with the **thing owned**, not the owner: *mi libro, mis libros, nuestra casa, nuestros amigos*. Only *nuestro* and *vuestro* have feminine forms.

**Su** is ambiguous (his, her, your, their). When it matters, use **de**: *el coche de Ana*, *la casa de mis padres*. Spanish has no apostrophe-s: *Ana's car* is *el coche de Ana*.

## Family, the classic test

*mi madre, mi padre, mis hermanos, tu abuela, su hijo, nuestros primos.*

## Demonstratives: this, that, that over there

| distance | masculine | feminine | plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| near me: this | **este** | **esta** | estos / estas |
| near you: that | **ese** | **esa** | esos / esas |
| far from both: that over there | **aquel** | **aquella** | aquellos / aquellas |

- *Este libro es mío.* (This book is mine.)
- *Esa chica es mi prima.* (That girl is my cousin.)
- *Aquellas montañas son los Pirineos.* (Those mountains over there are the Pyrenees.)

Without a noun they stand alone: *¿Cuál quieres? — Este.* And *esto / eso / aquello* refer to something unknown or an idea: *¿Qué es esto?*

## Every, each, all

**cada** never changes: *cada día, cada semana*. **todo** agrees: *todos los días, toda la clase, todas las chicas*.

vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother is eighty years old.

quiz.explanation: Possessives agree with the thing owned. Libros is plural, so mis.
hints: A plural noun takes a plural possessive.

quiz.prompt: Translate: Ana's car → el coche ___ Ana
quiz.explanation: Spanish uses de for possession: el coche de Ana.

quiz.prompt: ___ libro es mío. (this book, in my hand)

quiz.explanation: Far from both speakers takes aquel. The feminine plural is aquellas.

quiz.prompt: Complete: ___ chica es mi prima. (that girl, near you)
quiz.explanation: That near the listener is ese, and the feminine is esa.
hints: 'That' near the listener, feminine to match chica.

quiz.explanation: With los días, todo agrees: todos los días.

listening.text: Ese coche es de mi padre.
listening.note: Spanish has no apostrophe-s: el coche de mi padre.

listening.text: Nuestro perro come mucho todos los días.
listening.meaning: Our dog eats a lot every day.
listening.note: New word: el perro = the dog.

listening.text: Aquella casa blanca es de mis abuelos.
listening.meaning: That white house over there is my grandparents'.

listening.text: Mis primos viven en Sevilla con su madre.
listening.meaning: My cousins live in Seville with their mother.

listening.text: ¿Vuestros padres trabajan en Madrid todos los días?
listening.meaning: Do your parents work in Madrid every day?
listening.note: Vuestros agrees with padres, the thing owned.

listening.text: Mi prima Marta vive con sus padres y su abuela en Madrid.
listening.meaning: My cousin Marta lives with her parents and her grandmother in Madrid.

conversations.title: Whose is this?
conversations.scenario: At a family lunch, Clara explains who everyone is to her friend Leo.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Esta es mi abuela y aquel señor es mi abuelo.
lines.meaning: This is my grandmother and that man over there is my grandfather.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: And that girl? Is she your sister?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No, es mi prima. Sus padres viven en Cádiz.
lines.meaning: No, she's my cousin. Her parents live in Cádiz.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Es de mi abuela. Nuestra casa está en el centro.
lines.meaning: It's my grandmother's. Our house is in the centre.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Do you all eat here every Sunday?

bites.title: Agree with the thing
bites.rule: Possessives match what is owned, not who owns it: I own many books, so mis libros; we own one house, so nuestra casa.
bites.example: Mis libros están en nuestra casa.
bites.example_meaning: My books are in our house.

bites.title: Su has several meanings
bites.rule: Su/sus can mean his, her, their or your (formal). When it matters, switch to de. Spanish has no apostrophe-s: Ana's car is el coche de Ana.

bites.title: Here, there, way over there
bites.rule: Este is near me, ese is near you, aquel is far from both of us. Memory trick: este and estos have a T, like this and these.
bites.example: Este libro es mío y aquella casa es de mi abuela.
bites.example_meaning: This book is mine and that house over there is my grandmother's.

bites.title: Cada never changes
bites.rule: Cada never changes: cada día, cada semana. Todo changes to fit its noun: todos los días, toda la clase, todas las chicas.

sorts.title: Singular or plural possessive?
sorts.why: The possessive copies the number of the thing owned: one thing takes mi/tu/su, several things take mis/tus/sus.

sorts.title: Which form of nuestro?
sorts.why: Nuestro and vuestro match the gender and number of the thing owned, not of the owners.

sorts.title: Este, ese or aquel?
sorts.why: Distance decides. Use este near the speaker, ese near the listener and aquel far from both.

spots.why: Padres is plural, so the possessive is plural: mis.

spots.sentence: Nuestro casa está en el centro.
spots.why: Casa is feminine, and nuestro has a feminine form: nuestra.

spots.sentence: Ella vive con su dos hermanos.
spots.why: Su agrees with hermanos (plural), not with ella: sus.
Before a noun use este; esto stands alone for unknown things.

builds.text: Nuestra casa está en el centro.
builds.meaning: Our house is in the centre.
